newsitem.title: USA: IND. JUDGE DISMISSES ARENA LEGISLATION CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: IND. JUDGE DISMISSES ARENA LEGISLATION CHALLENGE.

text.p: A Marion County, Ind., judge on Wednesday dismissed a legal challenge to a new law that partly enables bond financing for a new Indiana Pacers arena.

Indiana Treasurer Joyce Brinkman had brought the challenge in June contending that the law violates single subject requirements by creating a local bond bank and permitting an annexation as well as enabling financing for $50 million of bonds for the new arena.
Superior Court Judge Cynthia Ayers ruled that Brinkman had no standing to bring the challenge and granted state Attorney General Jeff Modisett's motion to dismiss the lawsuit.
"Obviously, I am disappointed," Brinkman said, adding that had to review the decision before deciding on her next step.

The law created a special sports entertainment district in downtown Indianapolis to capture up to $5 million of state sales and income taxes anually to back $50 million of bonds for the planned $175 million arena.
